'''Patrick Couvreur''', born 1950 in [[Schaerbeek]] ([[Brussels]]),<ref name="ARMB">[http://www.armb.be/index.php?id=1384 Académie royale de Médecine de Belgique]</ref> is a [[French people|French]] [[pharmacologist]] who specialises in medical [[nanotechnology]] and is currently professor at the [[University of Paris-Sud]].<ref name=JDT/>

Couvreur was elected as a member into the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2015 for advances in nanomedicine and commercialization of targeted nanotechnology systems for cancer treatment.

== Biography ==
Patrick Couvreur obtained his Candidature in [[pharmaceutical science]] in 1969, at the [[University of Namur]],<ref name="UNamur">Patrick Couvreur,
pionnier en nanomédecine (UNamur) [http://www.unamur.be/services/sevrex/sevrexp/librecours/2011/libre-cours-79/lc79-p10] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305011908/http://www.unamur.be/services/sevrex/sevrexp/librecours/2011/libre-cours-79/lc79-p10 |date=2016-03-05 }}</ref> followed by a diploma in [[pharmacy]] in 1972, at the [[Catholic University of Louvain]] (UCL).<ref name=JDT /> He received a [[Doctorate]] in pharmaceutical science in 1975 from the same university,<ref name=JDT /> where he worked in the laboratory next door to the Belgian Nobel Prize winner,<ref>[http://www.lepoint.fr/futurapolis/coulisses/les-nanomedicaments-un-grand-espoir-pour-la-guerison-de-cancers-11-02-2012-1430528_532.php Le Point, 11 février 2012]</ref> [[Christian de Duve]], who was an inspiration for his subsequent career.<ref name="FT">[http://www.ft.com/intl/cms/s/0/cd285ce6-b70d-11e2-a249-00144feabdc0.html Financial Times, 28 May 2013]</ref>

From 1976 to 1977 he was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at [[ETH Zurich]], before joining the Catholic University of Louvain, first as a senior research assistant, and then as a senior researcher.<ref name=JDT />

In 1984 he was appointed to a professorship at the Institut Galien Paris Sud ([[University of Paris-Sud]]/[[CNRS]]).<ref name="Finfo">France Info, 14 septembre 2012</ref>

In 2009–2010, he held the Liliane Bettencourt Chair of Technological Innovation at the [[Collège de France]].<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/site/en-annual-chairs-previous/Chair-in-Technological-Innovation-Liliane-Bettencourt.htm
 |title=Chair in Technological Innovation Liliane Bettencourt - Annual Chairs
 |publisher=[[Collège de France]]
 |access-date=7 May 2017
}}</ref>

He has three children and several grandchildren.

== Principal achievements ==
Patrick Couvreur is known for his work in the field of [[drug vectorization]] for the treatment of [[cancer]].

In 1997 he founded BioAlliance,<ref>[http://www.lecho.be/actualite/archive/Patrick_Couvreur_un_inventeur_au_coeur_de_la_revolution_des_nanotechnologies.9351374-1802.art L'Echo, 29 mai 2013]</ref> a company that employs more than 60 people.<ref name="Finfo" /> In 2007, he founded Medsqual, a start-up that seeks to develop [[nanomedicine]]s based on [[squalene]]<ref name=EPO>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.epo.org/learning-events/european-inventor/finalists/2013/couvreur/feature.html
 |title=Fighting cancer with nanotechnology
 |publisher=[[European Patent Office]]
 |access-date=6 May 2019
 }}</ref>

== Prizes and distinctions ==
Patrick Couvreur was awarded the Prix Galien in 2009<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pharmaceutiques.com/phq/mag/pdf/phq169_120_industrie.pdf |title=Prix Galien 2009 Les Trois Laureates |access-date=2019-05-06 |archive-date=2010-12-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101219172643/http://pharmaceutiques.com/phq/mag/pdf/phq169_120_industrie.pdf }}</ref> for his work on "squalenization", a significant advance in drug vectorization that involves coupling an [[active ingredient]] with [[squalene]].<ref name = EPO/>  In the same year he received 2,2 million euros of funding from the [[European Research Council]] (ERC).<ref>[https://audiovisual.ec.europa.eu/en/video/I-077953 European Inventor Award 2013 - Patrick Couvreur (Research)]</ref>

On 20 June 2012, he shared the [[CNRS]] Innovation Medal with [[Alain Benoit]] and [[José-Alain Sahel]].<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.cnrs.fr/en/research/awards/innovation.htm
 |title=CNRS Innovation medalists
 |date=18 March 2018
 |publisher= [[CNRS]]
 |access-date= 6 May 2019
 }}</ref>

In 2013 Patrick Couvreur was awarded the [[European Inventor Award]] for his work on [[nanocapsules]] for cancer treatment.<ref name = EPO/>

Patrick Couvreur is a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]], the [[French Academy of Technologies]] the [[Académie Nationale de Médecine]] and the Académie de Pharmacie. He is also a foreign member of the [[National Academy of Medicine]] (USA), the [[National Academy of Engineering]] (USA), the Belgian Royal Academy of Medicine and the [[Real Academia Nacional de Farmacia]] (Spain).

On 31 December 2017, he was appointed a Chevalier of the [[Legion of Honor]].

In 2019, he received the [[Journal of Drug Targeting]]'s Lifetime Achievement Award.<ref name=JDT>{{cite journal
| last       = Akhtar
| first      = Saghir
| date       = 28 February 2019
| title      = In honour of Professor Patrick Couvreur, Recipient of the Journal of Drug Targeting's Lifetime Achievement Award for 2019
| journal    = Journal of Drug Targeting
| volume     = 27
| issue      = 5–6
| pages      = 467–468
| doi        = 10.1080/1061186X.2019.1589139
| pmid = 30816061
| doi-access= free
}}</ref>
